correctness.rationale: A double count gives \(2r\le3(15-r)\), hence at most nine flags. Equality supplies six perfect matchings of a nine-edge graph on six points. A complete case proof shows six perfect matchings occur only for \(K_{3,3}\); this forces the precise ten flagged matchings. Every flag belongs to two maxima, and transitivity of the partition action plus double-counting proves pairwise intersection one. Both independently constructed exact exhaustive verifiers passed. Finite code is corroborative, with unrestricted scope confined to this fixed graph.

value.rationale: A complete classification of all maximum induced matchings in the canonical thirty-vertex cubic girth-eight cage is a natural extremal structural problem. The forced vertex–edge incidence of \(K_{10}\) and pairwise equidistant code are nontrivial global consequences, and the exact eight-replacement threshold expresses configuration-space rigidity. Not merely an arbitrary finite slice or known colouring bound.
